title: Quarterly roadmap: responsive-capacity corridors and autoscale readiness
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Build a prescriptive quarter plan and runbook to introduce "responsive-capacity corridors" — a policy layer that codifies warm-pool reservation bands, fast-path surge lanes, and graceful degradation behaviors for Dedicated customers. The goal is to reduce P50/P95 tail latency during surges, lower emergency manual reserve top-ups, and provide predictable economic signals for customers and internal ops teams.
acceptance_criteria: Corridor policy spec reviewed and approved by eng & SRE
Playbook with 3 runbook scenarios (normal, surge, multi-region failover) published to Confluence
Canary test harness implemented to simulate surge patterns and measure latency/cost impact
Telemetry dashboards showing corridor adherence, cold-start rate, and cost delta available in Console within milestone window
Rollout plan with canary gating and rollback criteria signed off by Security & Legal (if applicable)
milestones: Engineering spike: simulation harness + autoscale policy prototype — 2026-02-28
decisions: Use a multi-tier corridor model (baseline warranted reservation + 2 surge bands) instead of single threshold to reduce oscillation
Prefer conservative warm-pool sizing with explicit economic guardrails rather than fully predictive automatic top-ups for initial rollout
Expose corridor hints to customers via Console but keep automatic scaling actions controlled by ops for first two quarters
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Initial spec posted to Confluence (link in docs_links). Requested capacity math review from Runtime team.
2026-02-16: Runtime engineering completed a micro-benchmark showing 8% cost saving with corridor-level KV cache reuse in moderate surge workloads.
2026-02-19: SRE raised a concern about cross-region warm-pool consistency during failover — added a mitigation task.
2026-02-20: Product leadership approved P1 priority and allocated a 2-week spike in Cycle 48 for engineering to prove canary harness
open_tasks: ENG-21432: Implement simulation harness for burst patterns (assigned)
ENG-21590: Add corridor metrics to Console telemetry pipeline (depends on PR #1423)
PM-872001: Customer communication draft for beta customers
SRE-9002: Run cross-region failover rehearsal and capture gap report
risks: Over-optimizing warm pools could increase baseline costs for low-util customers
Incorrect corridor sizing may trigger oscillatory autoscale behavior leading to SLA violations
Insufficient telemetry may make rollback decisions ambiguous during canaries
mitigation: Start with conservative sizing and explicit guardrails; iterate after measured canaries
Implement hysteresis and cooldown windows in autoscale policies to prevent rapid oscillation
Define clear rollback criteria (latency > SLO by 15% for 5 minutes OR error rate spike > 3x baseline)
notes: This ticket is intended to be a compact program-level artifact that maps OKR-level success to actionable engineering milestones. Aim for a minimally invasive first release that proves the corridor model and opens the door for automated predictive top-ups in Q3.
communication_plan: Beta cohort invites to 5 existing dedicated customers + ops-run workshops. Release notes in Console and a dedicated changelog entry.
hand_off_criteria: Playbook live in Confluence, runbook tested in staging, dashboards green for 48 hours with canary traffic, and cross-team signoff recorded in PR comment threads.
postmortem_plan: If canary fails, run a 72-hour incident review with SRE and Runtime, capture RCA, and schedule corrective engineering in next cycle.
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers: focus on corridor sizing assumptions (section 2 of spec) and canary simulation fidelity. Provide comments in Confluence page or tag in Slack channel #dedicated-capacity.
estimated_cost_impact: Initial conservative estimate: +2% baseline cost for warm pools, expected net -6% cost per token during surge windows after cache reuse optimizations
